clauses.text: There shall be a National Procuremen Commission (in this Chapter referred to as the “Commission consisting of five members appointed by the President o the recommendation of the Constitutional Council, o whom at least three members shall be persons who hav had proven experience in procurement, accountancy, la or public administration. The President shall, on the rec ommendation of the Constitutional Council, appoint on member as the Chairman of the Commission.

Every member of the Commission shall hol office for a period of three years from the date of appointmen unless such member earlier resigns from office by a writin addressed to the President or is removed from office by th President for causes assigned with the approval of th Constitutional Council or is convicted by a court of law fo an offence involving moral turpitude or is elected as a Memb of Parliament or as a member of a Provincial Council o of a local authority or if a resolution for the imposition of civic disability on him is passed in terms of Article 81.

The Chairman and every member of th Commission shall be paid such allowances as may b determined by a resolution of Parliament. Such allowance shall be charged on the Consolidated Fund and shall not b diminished during the term of office of such Chairman o the member.

It shall be the function of the Commissio to formulate fair, equitable, transparent, competitive and co effective procedures and guidelines, for the procurement o goods and services, works, consultancy services an information systems by government institutions and caus titution of the Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka such guidelines to be published in the Gazette and within three months of such publications, to be placed before Parliament.

Without prejudice to the generality of paragraph (1), it shall be the function of the Commission to - (a) monitor and report to the appropriate authorities, on whether all procurement of goods and services, works, consultancy services and information systems by government institutions are based on procurement plans prepared in accordance with previously approved action plans; (b) monitor and report to the appropriate authorities on whether all qualified bidders for the provision of goods and services, works, consultancy services and information systems by government institutions are afforded an equal opportunity to participate in the bidding process for the provision of those goods and services, works, consultancy services and infor- mation systems; (c) monitor and report to the appropriate authorities on whether the procedures for the selection of contractors, and the awarding of contracts for the provision of goods and services, works, consultancy services and information systems to Government institutions, are fair and transparent; (d) report on whether members of Procurement Committees and Technical Evaluation Committees relating to the procurements, appointed by government institutions are suitably qualified; and (e) investigate reports of procurements made b government institutions outside establishe procedures and guidelines, and to report th officers responsible for such procurements the relevant authorities for necessary action.

The Commission may, by Notice in writin require any person to - (a) attend before the Commission, to be question be the Commission; (b) produce to the Commission, any document thing in the possession or control of th person and specified in such Notice.

Every person who - (a) fails, without reasonable cause to appear befo the Commission when required to do so by Notice sent to him under paragraph (1); (b) appears before the Commission in complian with such a Notice, but refuses witho reasonable cause, to answer any questions p to him by the Commission; or (c) fails or refuses, without reasonable cause, produce any document or thing which he w required to produce by a Notice sent to hi under paragraph (1), commits an offence and shall on conviction be liab to a fine not exceeding one hundred thousand rupees or imprisonment for a term not exceeding seven years, or both such fine and imprisonment. titution of the Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka
Every High Court established under Article 154P of the Constitution shall have jurisdiction to hear and deter- mine any matter referred to in paragraph (2).
The Commission shall meet as often as may be necessary for the discharge of its functions.

The Chairman shall preside at all meetings of the Commission. In the absence of the Chairman from any meeting of the Commission, the members present shall elect a Chairman for that meeting, from among themselves. (3)The quorum for any meeting of the Commission shall be three.

Decisions of the Commission shall be by the majority vote of the members present and voting at the meeting at which the decision is taken, and in the event of an equality of votes, the Chairman or member presiding at the meeting shall have a casting vote.
Subject to the preceding provisions of this Article, the Commission may determine the procedure with regard to its meetings and the transaction of business at such meetings.

The Commission shall have the power to act notwithstanding any vacancy in the membership of the Commission, and no act, proceeding or decision of the Commission shall be invalid or deemed to be invalid, by reason only of such vacancy of defect in the appointment of a member.

clauses.text: The Commission shall appoint a Secretary-General and such other officers as it may consider necessary for the proper discharge of its functions, on such terms and conditions as may be determined by the Commission.
All members and officers of the Commissi shall be deemed to be public servants within the meanin and for the purpose of, Chapter IX of the Penal Co (Chapter 19).

No suit, prosecution or other proceeding shall against any member or officer of the Commission for a act or thing which in good faith is done or purported to done by him in the performance of his duties or t discharge of his functions, under the Constitution.
